master: Logo design presentation board for KARMAN PREP, a premium SAT preparation company for well-off families: small live cohorts that each end on one specific SAT test date, private one-on-one tutoring over Zoom, and a daily digital practice app. The name comes from the Karman line, the boundary 100 km up where the sky ends and space begins: the line you rise past. Design it the way Allan Peters (author of Logos That Last) designs brand marks: one bold, simple, geometric mark built from heavy strokes of one even weight, merging the capital letter K with the Karman line (a single horizontal line) and at most one more idea into one inseparable, ownable shape. Use one of his tools: negative space, overlapping geometry, visual rhythm, an unexpected twist on a familiar shape, or visual flow. Crisp vector edges, generous internal spacing, no thin hairlines, so it reads clearly at 16 pixels and in one colour. Layout: pure black artwork on a plain white background. On the left, the brand mark alone, large. On the right, a horizontal lockup: the same mark followed by the wordmark KARMAN PREP in custom-drawn geometric capital letters whose stroke weight matches the mark (not a stock typeface), spelled exactly K-A-R-M-A-N P-R-E-P, with generous letter spacing. Flat 2D vector only. No gradients, no shadows, no 3D, no texture, no paper or device mockup, no colour, no other text, no tagline. Avoid clichés: no graduation caps, owls, books, pencils, lightbulbs, rockets, ringed planets, swooshes, globes or shooting stars. The feeling: established, calm and confident, like an old institution with a modern edge. Not playful, not techy, not a startup app icon.
concepts: Thin Air
Concept: below the Karman line the K is solid; above the line the K breaks into horizontal stripes that get thinner and further apart as they rise, the way air thins with altitude (visual rhythm).
Lifted

Concept: the K is cut cleanly by one horizontal line through its upper third and the upper part is lifted slightly; the thin horizontal gap is the Karman line itself and continues a short distance beyond the letter on both sides (negative space).
Apogee
Concept: the upper arm of the K is a launch trajectory that curves upward through a thin horizontal line and levels off at its highest point, like the top of a flight path (visual flow).
Open Sky

Concept: one horizontal line crosses the K's upper third; below the line the K is solid black, above it the K is drawn only as a heavy outline, so past the line the letter becomes open sky (unexpected twist).
Planet Edge

Concept: the K stands over the gently curved edge of the earth seen from high above; where the letter overlaps the curved shape the black and white invert, and one arc just above the curve marks the edge of space (overlapping geometry).
Altimeter
Concept: the stem of the K is an altitude scale made of evenly spaced horizontal bars, and exactly one bar extends far to the left as the Karman line (visual rhythm).
Split Seal

Concept: a circular emblem divided by one horizontal line; the K crosses the line and inverts from black to white between the two halves. Minimal, like a modern version of an old institution's seal (overlapping geometry).
Square Cut

Concept: a solid black square with softly rounded corners; the K is cut out of it in negative space, and the horizontal Karman line is also cut through the square and flows into the K's upper arm (negative space).
Wordmark Line

Concept: a wordmark-led logo. Custom lettering for KARMAN where one horizontal line runs through the whole word at cap height and only the two A's rise through it; the brand mark is a compact K monogram drawn from the same lettering with the same line.
Designer's Choice
Concept: your own strongest idea combining the capital K and a single horizontal line the letter rises past, so that the line and the K become one shape that could not exist without each other.
